comment: The authoritative map from (governed tool, producer status) to the classification every client must apply. Derived from the producer, not from prose: GovernedStatusContractTests parses the McpCore case body for each tool and fails when a status it can emit has no entry here, and when an entry names a status the producer cannot emit. Both the C# and TypeScript consumers read this one file, so a shape neither of us modelled becomes a build error rather than a review round. Written after four consecutive review rounds on hand-written predicates, each of which found a producer shape the author had not modelled.

classifications.ran: The operation executed. Its rows are evidence and its counts are claims the client may render, subject to the response-shape rules.
classifications.capability_refused: The publisher declined a governed filter. It contributes a typed limitation and no rows. It does not make the response incomplete.
classifications.terminal_refusal: An authoritative non-capability refusal scoped to the request. It contributes no rows and no limitation, and it does not make the response incomplete, because the publisher answered definitely.
classifications.mode_unavailable: The requested retrieval mode is not authorized for this publisher. It contributes no rows and must never select filter-refusal copy.
classifications.invalid: Not emitted by the producer for this tool. Reaching this classification means the response did not come from the producer contract, so it can authorize neither rows nor absence claims.

shape_rules.comment: Shape requirements for a ran response, stated once. A ran envelope failing any of these is invalid, because the producer never emits it: the client must not silently narrow the evidence instead.

status_invariants.no_changes_in_period: works_changed == 0 and new_versions == 0 and changes is empty

status_invariants.no_result: total_works_in_force == 0 and works is empty and ambiguous_works is empty

paging_note: Zero rows beside a positive count is ORDINARY, not contradictory: in_force_on drains one remaining limit across publishers and changes_in_period slices one globally merged page while each publisher reports its own full total. Only the impossible directions are contradictions: rows exceeding the count, rows plus ambiguity units exceeding it, and rows beside a zero count.
